title: The Shockingly Simple Math Behind Early Retirement
summary: Blog post and comment thread arguing that savings rate alone sets years to financial independence, with readers debating return assumptions, the 4% rule and mortgages.

assertions.quote: your time to reach retirement depends on only one factor

verdicts.note: Mathematically true under constant real returns and equal spending before and after, but low incomes hit a fixed-cost floor that limits achievable savings rates.

assertions.quote: cutting your spending rate is much more powerful than increasing your income

verdicts.note: A permanent spending cut reduces the required nest egg and raises the savings rate at once, which the retirement arithmetic confirms.

assertions.quote: If want to retire within 10 years, the formula is right there in front of you – simply live on 35% of your take-home pay

verdicts.note: Follows from the model at 5% real returns and a 4% withdrawal rate; lower realized returns or higher withdrawal risk stretch the timeline.

assertions.quote: live off of the 4% safe withdrawal rate after retirement, with some flexibility in your spending during recessions

verdicts.note: The 4% rule came from 30-year US historical tests; for 50-year horizons and global data, failure rates rise and many analyses suggest nearer 3-3.5% without flexibility.

assertions.quote: You can earn 5% investment returns after inflation during your saving years

verdicts.note: US equities averaged roughly 6-7% real over a century and global equities about 5%, but mixed portfolios and high starting valuations deliver less.

assertions.quote: every extra principal payment gives you essentially a risk-free return on that amount of the mortgage rate

verdicts.note: Avoided interest is a guaranteed pre-tax return at the loan rate, less any lost interest deduction.

assertions.quote: you CAN tap 401k / IRA money before 59 1/2 without penalty

verdicts.note: US tax code section 72(t) allows penalty-free SEPP withdrawals; Roth conversion ladders are another route.

assertions.quote: point to real equity returns in the 2 to 4 percent range for the next 5-10 years

verdicts.note: Valuation measures like CAPE have modest predictive power for 10-year returns, though realized 2012-2022 US returns beat those forecasts.

assertions.quote: these will easily beat 5% returns after inflation

verdicts.note: Leveraged rentals bought after a crash have beaten stocks for some owners, but returns are highly local and depend on unpaid landlord labor.

assertions.quote: allow some slack in your budget for increased health expenses as you get older

verdicts.note: Health spending rises with age and children's costs vary, though work-related expenses fall after retirement, so the net effect is uncertain.

assertions.quote: super hard for the vast majority of people to have the investment discipline to stick with equity investments

verdicts.note: Investor-return studies consistently find a behavior gap of roughly one to two percentage points a year from poorly timed flows.

assertions.quote: The biggest thing I’d suggest against is day trading. Not worth the risk or time.

verdicts.note: Brokerage-record studies in the US, Taiwan and Brazil find the large majority of individual day traders lose money after costs, and only a few percent earn more than minimum wage.
